full_llm_interaction_log.purpose: Validate dataset choice for reproducing IEThresh experiments
full_llm_interaction_log.prompt: I want to reproduce the IEThresh algorithm from Donmez et al. (KDD 2009) and I'm thinking of using the UCI Mushroom dataset. The paper uses datasets with binary classification. Mushroom is binary (edible vs poisonous) and has 8124 instances. Is this a reasonable choice or should I pick something else?
full_llm_interaction_log.how_it_helped: Confirmed that Mushroom is a reasonable choice — binary classification, decent size, categorical features. Also mentioned that the paper uses datasets where noisy labels would have a meaningful impact, and Mushroom fits since the features are informative enough that a classifier can learn from it.
full_llm_interaction_log.student_verification: Checked the paper's Section 5 where they describe their experimental datasets. They use binary classification UCI datasets of similar size. Mushroom fits the criteria.

full_llm_interaction_log.purpose: Help with loading and preprocessing mushroom data
full_llm_interaction_log.prompt: How do I load the mushroom dataset from UCI and preprocess it for sklearn? The features are all categorical so I need to encode them. Also the paper doesn't mention any specific preprocessing so I just need something standard.
full_llm_interaction_log.how_it_helped: Gave me a snippet using pandas to load the CSV and one-hot encode with pd.get_dummies(). I didn't use the code directly but followed the same approach with my own variable names and added a train-test split matching the paper's protocol.
full_llm_interaction_log.student_verification: Ran the preprocessing pipeline and verified the output shapes and label distribution matched what I expected from the UCI dataset description page.
full_llm_interaction_log.student_modification: Rewrote the loading code with my own structure, added stratified train-test split (80-20) to match the paper's evaluation setup, and added a random seed for reproducibility.
